newsitem.title: FRANCE: All but two Corsicans held in French raid cleared.
newsitem.headline: All but two Corsicans held in French raid cleared.

text.p: French police suffered an embarrassing setback on Friday when all but two of 12 Corsicans seized after a bomb attack on Prime Minister Alain Juppe's mayoral offices were cleared of suspicion.

Justice sources said only two of those detained were liable for prosecution over the October 5 bombing carried out by Corsican separatists on the city hall in the southern city of Bordeaux, where Juppe is mayor.
Both were transferred to Paris where an anti-terrorism magistrate was likely to open a formal investigation against them on Sunday or Monday.
They were named as Jean-Jacques Cantara, seized in Bonifacio on the southern tip of Corsica, and Jacques-Marie Cantara, arrested in Marseille in southern France.

Five women detained in Thursday's police swoops were freed within hours and the sources said five other men were cleared for lack of evidence but they remained in custody, partly on suspicion of illegal possession of weapons.
Juppe has vowed to crack down on two decades of separatist guerrilla violence on Corsica after attacks spilled over onto the French mainland.
Justice sources said earlier a fugitive Corsican separatist leader had sought state compensation for an unsolved murder attempt against him in May 1995.
Francois Santoni, 36, was seriously wounded and his bodyguard was killed when they were shot while riding a motorcycle near the Corsican capital Ajaccio.

Santoni leads the Cuncolta Naziunalista, a political party and legal front for the main hardline separatist group, the Historic Wing of the outlawed Corsican National Liberation Front (FLNC) which claimed responsibility for the Bordeaux bombing.

He was sentenced this month in his absence to four months in jail for carrying guns and has been in hiding in the Corsican hills, saying he feared rival nationalist gunmen eager to settle past blood feuds.
French law says victims of unsolved crimes are eligible for compensation. But such a payment would not be automatic if a politically-motivated act of terror was involved.
A committee responsible for deciding Satoni's eligibility for compensation has asked prosecutors in Paris handling the investigation for advice on the case, the justice sources said.
